exposure: COVID-19 pandemic period (early-, peak-, and late-pandemic)
outcome: preexisting conditions (type 2 diabetes, chronic hypertension, gestational diabetes, preeclampsia)
cohort: The study included 7431 pregnant people with obesity (54% Black) who delivered at a large women's specialty hospital in Louisiana between 2018 and 2022.
finding: Black pregnant people with obesity started pregnancy with higher weight and more preexisting conditions but experienced lower gestational weight gain compared to White pregnant people, demonstrating exacerbated health disparities during pregnancy.
